decisions.reason: An accelerator program is only loosely related to the firm's core absorptive base in recycling machinery and process engineering, so management is likely to reallocate resources toward products where its existing technical knowledge can be applied more directly and scaled commercially.

Although a bio-based bitumen binder is somewhat farther from the firm's machinery core, its flagship status and links to waste-derived feedstocks give the firm enough related knowledge and incentive to continue learning and refining it rather than exit quickly.

An infectious waste decontamination plant fits closely with the firm's established capabilities in modular treatment systems, engineering, and commercialization, so absorptive capacity is high and continued market presence is likely.

A mobile mechanical recycling plant is strongly aligned with the firm's existing recycling expertise, manufacturing know-how, and decentralized-system strategy, making it the kind of product management would be most likely to retain and build on.
